learn.title: Two things tell you a lot
learn.body: A polynomial's degree and the sign of its leading coefficient decide how its graph ends on the far left and far right. Its zeros, the $x$-values where $f(x)=0$, tell you where the graph meets the $x$-axis.

learn.title: End behavior rules
learn.body: Even degree: both ends go the same way, up if the leading coefficient is positive, down if negative. Odd degree: the ends go opposite ways. Positive leading coefficient means down on the left and up on the right. Negative flips it.

learn.title: Zeros of $f(x)=x^3-4x$
learn.body: Factor, then set each factor to zero.
steps: Degree 3, leading coefficient $+1$: down on the left, up on the right.

learn.title: Repeated zeros
learn.body: In $(x-3)^2(x+1)$ the factor $x-3$ appears twice. At $x=3$ the graph touches the axis and turns back. At a zero with an odd count, such as $x=-1$, the graph crosses.
A polynomial of degree $n$ has at most $n$ real zeros and at most $n-1$ turning points.

questions.prompt: A polynomial has degree 4 and leading coefficient $+3$. How do its ends behave?
questions.explanation: Even degree means both ends match. A positive leading coefficient sends them up.

questions.prompt: For $f(x)=-2x^3+x$, what happens as $x$ gets very large and positive?
questions.explanation: Odd degree with a negative leading coefficient is up on the left and down on the right.

questions.prompt: How many real zeros does $f(x)=(x-1)(x+3)(x-5)$ have?
questions.explanation: Each factor gives one zero: $1$, $-3$ and $5$.

questions.prompt: A degree 5 polynomial with a positive leading coefficient goes \_\_ on the far left.
questions.explanation: Odd degree means opposite ends. Up on the right means down on the left.

questions.prompt: Match each function to its end behavior.
questions.explanation: Even degree gives matching ends, odd degree gives opposite ends, and a negative sign flips the picture.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest zero of $x^3-4x$?
questions.explanation: The zeros are $-2$, $0$ and $2$. The smallest is $-2$.

questions.prompt: What does the graph of $(x-3)^2(x+1)$ do at $x=3$?
choices: Touches the axis and turns back
questions.explanation: The factor $x-3$ is squared, so the zero repeats. The graph touches the axis there and turns.

questions.prompt: Find the zeros of $x^3-4x$. Put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: Factor completely first. Then the zero product rule lets you set each factor to zero.

questions.prompt: What is the largest number of turning points a degree 4 polynomial can have?
questions.explanation: A degree $n$ polynomial has at most $n-1$ turning points, so at most 3.
